note_sentences.text: Patient is a 67-year-old male presenting with progressive dyspnea and bilateral lower extremity edema over the past two weeks.
He has a history of ischemic cardiomyopathy with LVEF of 25% on last echocardiogram six months ago.
Current medications include lisinopril 10mg daily, carvedilol 25mg twice daily, and furosemide 40mg daily.
On examination, jugular venous distension is present with bilateral crackles on lung auscultation and 2+ pitting edema bilaterally.
Vitals: BP 108/72, HR 92, RR 22, SpO2 93% on room air, Temp 36.8C.
Labs drawn on admission include CBC, BMP, and BNP pending.
Chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral pleural effusions and vascular congestion consistent with pulmonary edema.
The patient was seen in the cardiology clinic three weeks ago with stable symptoms at that time.

answer_sentences.text: The patient presents with acute decompensated heart failure, supported by progressive dyspnea, bilateral edema, and known cardiomyopathy.
Physical examination findings of JVD, bilateral crackles, and peripheral edema are consistent with volume overload.

note_sentences.text: A 54-year-old female was admitted for evaluation of recurrent episodes of syncope over the past month.
Electrocardiogram reveals third-degree AV block with a ventricular rate of 38 bpm.
Transthoracic echocardiogram shows preserved LVEF of 55% with no significant valvular disease.
The patient denies chest pain, palpitations, or recent changes in medication.
Holter monitoring over 48 hours confirmed intermittent complete heart block with pauses up to 4.2 seconds.
She has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes, well-controlled on current regimen.

answer_sentences.text: The patient has symptomatic complete heart block as demonstrated by third-degree AV block on ECG.
Holter monitoring confirms intermittent complete heart block with significant pauses, supporting the need for pacemaker implantation.

note_sentences.text: A 72-year-old male presents to the ED with acute onset right-sided weakness and speech difficulty beginning 2 hours ago.
Past medical history is significant for atrial fibrillation, for which he takes warfarin irregularly.
CT head without contrast shows no acute intracranial hemorrhage.
His INR on admission is 1.2, subtherapeutic for stroke prophylaxis.
NIHSS score is 14, indicating a moderate-to-severe stroke.
The patient lives alone and his daughter reports he often forgets to take his medications.
CTA head and neck reveals occlusion of the left middle cerebral artery M1 segment.

answer_sentences.text: The patient presents with an acute ischemic stroke, likely cardioembolic given his history of atrial fibrillation and subtherapeutic anticoagulation.
His elevated NIHSS score and MCA occlusion indicate he is a candidate for acute intervention.

note_sentences.text: A 45-year-old female presents with progressively worsening fatigue and unintentional weight loss of 15 lbs over 3 months.
Laboratory evaluation reveals TSH < 0.01 mIU/L and free T4 of 4.8 ng/dL, consistent with overt hyperthyroidism.
Radioactive iodine uptake scan shows diffusely increased uptake at 24 hours.
The patient reports occasional palpitations but denies eye symptoms or skin changes.
Family history is notable for autoimmune thyroid disease in her mother and sister.

answer_sentences.text: The patient has Graves disease, confirmed by overt hyperthyroidism on labs with diffusely increased radioactive iodine uptake.

note_sentences.text: A 58-year-old male with COPD presents with increased sputum production and worsening dyspnea over the past 5 days.
He completed a course of azithromycin prescribed by his PCP 2 weeks ago for a similar episode.
Arterial blood gas shows pH 7.32, pCO2 55 mmHg, pO2 58 mmHg, and HCO3 28 mEq/L on 2L nasal cannula.
Chest CT reveals hyperinflated lungs with upper lobe predominant emphysema and no acute consolidation.
Pulmonary function tests from 6 months ago showed FEV1 of 35% predicted, consistent with GOLD stage III.
Sputum culture obtained on admission grows Pseudomonas aeruginosa, sensitive to piperacillin-tazobactam.
The patient has a 40-pack-year smoking history and quit 2 years ago.
He is currently on tiotropium, fluticasone-salmeterol, and albuterol PRN.

answer_sentences.text: ABG demonstrates acute-on-chronic respiratory acidosis with hypoxemia, indicating a severe COPD exacerbation requiring close monitoring.
Sputum culture growing Pseudomonas guides targeted antibiotic therapy for this infectious exacerbation.

note_sentences.text: A 63-year-old female presents with a 3-day history of right upper quadrant pain radiating to the right shoulder.
She has had two prior episodes of biliary colic, both managed conservatively.
WBC count is 14,200/uL with 82% neutrophils and total bilirubin is 1.8 mg/dL.
Abdominal ultrasound reveals a distended gallbladder with wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid, and a 2.1 cm stone impacted in the gallbladder neck.
Murphy sign is positive on physical examination, and the patient is febrile at 38.6C.
She has no known drug allergies and takes lisinopril and metformin.

answer_sentences.text: The clinical presentation and imaging findings are consistent with acute cholecystitis requiring surgical consultation.
Ultrasound confirms gallbladder pathology with an impacted stone and signs of inflammation, and the positive Murphy sign supports the diagnosis.
